official.description: The Holland Scholarship, also called the NL Scholarship, is a Dutch government-funded award co-funded by participating universities and administered at school level at Erasmus University Rotterdam. EUR's institute pages document a EUR 5,000 award granted to one student per school on the basis of academic excellence, while the university's central pages list wider funding for incoming students and point applicants to Study in NL. It is a flat contribution towards study costs rather than full funding.
official.program_type: Government and university co-funded first-year scholarship for non-EEA master's students

verification.notes: The EUR 5,000 figure and the not-a-full-tuition-scholarship wording come from the Institute for Housing and Urban Development Studies page, part of Erasmus University Rotterdam. The university's central scholarships pages confirm the two-track set-up for students coming to Rotterdam versus students going abroad and the faculty-level variation in programmes and deadlines.

applicant_utility.summary: The Holland Scholarship or NL Scholarship is a flat EUR 5,000 contribution towards studying in Rotterdam, and IHS is blunt that it is not a full-tuition scholarship, so treat it as a discount on a bill you will largely pay yourself. Because each school runs its own round and its own deadline, the practical move is to work backwards from the school: get your admission letter first, then file the scholarship documents by that school's date, which at IHS is 25 April for the programme application due 15 April. The IHS document list is exacting on money, asking for a bank statement covering twelve times EUR 1,250 plus a statement of how much you and your family will personally contribute, so start that financial evidence early because it is the part that stalls applicants.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EEA master's students who already have or will soon have an unconditional admission letter from an EUR school, and who can show genuine financial need alongside a strong grade list.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify which EUR faculty or school runs your programme and open its own scholarship page, not only the central list
Secure the unconditional admission letter first, since it is a mandatory attachment
Ask your university for a certified copy of the bachelor degree including the grade list rather than a photocopy
Prepare a motivation letter that clearly outlines the career path after the programme, as the school requires
Prepare the financial file: a bank statement from you, your parents or your sponsors, plus a statement of the maximum contribution you can make
Note the decision date for your school, at IHS 3 May, and plan visa and housing applications around it
common_rejection_risks: Waiting for the central EUR deadline instead of the school-level date, which varies
Missing the unconditional admission letter requirement by applying only for a conditional offer
Submitting a CV-style motivation letter without the required career path outline
Providing uncertified grade lists, which the school requires to be certified
Assuming the EUR 5,000 pays tuition, when the school states it is not a full-tuition scholarship
Overlooking the required statement of your own contribution, which is an explicit document
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Most of the non-EEA tuition fee, plus rent, food, transport, health insurance and visa costs; the bank statement requirement of twelve times EUR 1,250 gives a rough floor for the living-cost need the award does not cover.
document_audit: The degree and grade list need certification, so allow a week or two at your home institution
Bank statements from parents or sponsors are accepted, but the statement of your maximum contribution must still be explicit
If your admission letter is conditional, hold the application until it becomes unconditional rather than submitting an ineligible file
alerts: One award per school per round, so this is a single-slot competition decided once
Deadlines move per school, and IHS already publishes the 2027 dates while other faculties may not yet
Check the faculty-level pages for additional EUR funds such as the Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship, which covers tuition and support on a different scale
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the programme at your EUR school by its deadline, then submit the NL Scholarship documents with the admission letter and financial evidence to that school by its own scholarship deadline, and await the school's decision date.
